questions.question: A therapist modifies a wheelchair to allow the rear wheels to be moved backward by approximately two inches. This type of modification would be most beneficial to a patient with:
questions.explanation: With bilateral lower-limb amputations the centre of gravity shifts backward, so the rear axle is moved back to prevent tipping.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: Type of nerve lesion in Saturday night palsy most commonly is:
questions.explanation: Saturday night palsy is usually neurapraxia of the radial nerve.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: Assuming normal development, which activity would typically not occur prior to nine months of age?
questions.explanation: A neat pincer grasp develops at about 9 to 12 months.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A patient with a spinal cord injury positioned on a tilt table elevated to 60 degrees begins to complain of dizziness and nausea. The therapist's most immediate response should be to: 6

options.A: Lower the tilt table 10 degrees and take off the patient's abdominal binder
options.B: Leave the tilt table at 60 degrees and call for medical assistance
options.C: Monitor the patient's vital signs with the tilt table at 60 degrees and continue to elevate the table as tolerated
options.D: Lower the tilt table to horizontal and monitor the patient's vital signs

questions.explanation: Lower the tilt table to horizontal and monitor vital signs when symptoms of hypotension occur.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: Dependent bed mobility is a realistic goal for a patient with C6 tetraplegia. In order to achieve this goal, a physical therapist should initiate strengthening to all of the following muscles except the:
questions.explanation: In C6 tetraplegia flexor carpi ulnaris is not innervated (C7-C8), so it is not a strengthening target for bed mobility.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: In designing a wheelchair for a patient with bilateral transfemoral amputations, the axle should be moved in what direction?
questions.explanation: The rear axle is moved back for bilateral transfemoral amputees to prevent tipping.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: Which aquatic exercise would be the most effective in reducing tone in a patient with a spinal cord injury?

options.A: Slow passive movements of the neck and upper extremities with the patient floating in supine
options.B: Passive abduction and adduction of the upper extremities with the patient in short sitting
options.C: Approximation of the trunk with the patient floating in supine
options.D: Gentle rocking of the trunk with the patient in short sitting

questions.explanation: Slow passive movements while floating in warm water relax muscles and reduce tone.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A physical therapist assists a patient with C7 tetraplegia into a prone on elbows position on a mat. The therapist instructs the patient to push his elbows down, tuck his chin, and lift his trunk off of the mat while rounding out the shoulders. This exercise is helpful in strengthening the:
questions.explanation: Pushing down through the elbows in prone strengthens serratus anterior and scapular stabilisers.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A physical therapist treats a patient with incomplete L4 paraplegia. The therapist uses proprioceptive neuromuscular facilitation techniques to strengthen the abdominals and improve trunk stability in sitting. The most appropriate technique to improve strength and control include:

options.D: Alternating isometrics and timing for emphasis in sitting

questions.explanation: Alternating isometrics and timing for emphasis improve trunk stability and strength in sitting.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A patient with a C3 spinal cord injury is positioned in supine. Which area is most susceptible to pressure in this position?
questions.explanation: In supine the sacrum is most susceptible to pressure.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A physical therapist performs passive range of motion to a patient with C7 tetraplegia. The patient's bilateral straight leg raise is measured passively to 90 degrees. What should 10 the physical therapist conclude about the patient's ability to perform activities of daily living?

options.A: The patient requires a straight leg raise of 110-120 degrees in order to perform long sit and activities of daily living
options.B: The patient is at a functional range to perform long sit and activities of daily living
options.C: The patient's range of motion is beyond the expected limit for long sit and activities of daily living
options.D: The patient requires a straight leg raise of 150 degrees in order to perform long sit and activities of daily living

questions.explanation: Long sitting needs about 110-120 degrees of straight leg raise, so 90 degrees is inadequate.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A patient diagnosed with an incomplete spinal cord lesion that presents with muscle paralysis on the ipsilateral side of the lesion and a loss of pain, temperature, and sensitivity on the contralateral side of the lesion describes:
questions.explanation: Ipsilateral paralysis with contralateral pain and temperature loss is Brown-Sequard syndrome.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: What is the first functional task that should be taught to a patient with a T2 spinal cord injury?
questions.explanation: Rolling is the first functional skill taught after thoracic spinal cord injury.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A patient rehabilitating from a spinal cord injury works on self-range of motion activities in sitting. Suddenly, the patient begins to demonstrate signs and symptoms of autonomic dysreflexia. The most appropriate therapist action is to:

options.A: Keep the patient in sitting, monitor blood pressure, and check the bowel and bladder for impairment
options.B: Lie the patient flat, monitor blood pressure, and check the bowel and bladder for impairment
options.C: Lie the patient flat, monitor blood pressure, and give the patient fluids
options.D: Keep the patient sitting, monitor blood pressure, wait for medical assistance

questions.explanation: Keep the patient sitting to lower blood pressure, check bladder and bowel, and monitor BP.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: Commonest cause of paraplegia:
questions.explanation: Trauma is the commonest cause of paraplegia.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: Peripheral nerves can withstand ischemia up to:
questions.explanation: Peripheral nerves tolerate ischaemia for about one hour before conduction fails.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: Radial nerve injury of this type recovers with conservative management:
questions.explanation: Neurapraxia recovers spontaneously with conservative management.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A therapist working in an acute care hospital examines a patient that sustained a CVA two-day ago. The therapist positions the patient in sidelying on the hemiplegic side. Which of the following is not a benefit of positioning on the hemiplegic side?

options.A: Reduces spasticity through elongation of the hemiplegic side
options.B: Allows the unaffected extremity to reach and perform functional tasks
options.C: Increases the influence of tonic neck and labyrinthine reflexes
options.D: Enhances proprioceptive awareness of the hemiplegic side through weight bearing

questions.explanation: Side-lying on the hemiplegic side does not increase tonic neck and labyrinthine reflex influence.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A 12-year-old female that became anoxic in a near drowning performs dynamic activities in quadruped. The next posture to attain in the developmental sequence is:
questions.explanation: After quadruped the developmental sequence progresses to tall kneeling.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A physical therapist examines a neurological patient with a flaccid left side. In order to facilitate muscular activity, the treatment plan should include:
questions.explanation: Weight bearing, tapping and approximation facilitate tone in a flaccid limb.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A therapist conducts reflex testing on a patient with a traumatic brain injury. Which stimulus should the therapist utilize to test for clonus at the ankle?

options.C: Passive, rapid dorsiflexion of the ankle
options.D: Passive, slow dorsiflexion of the ankle

questions.explanation: Clonus at the ankle is elicited by a rapid passive dorsiflexion.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A patient diagnosed with pure athetoid cerebral palsy would most likely demonstrate:

options.A: Disturbed sense of balance and faulty depth perception

questions.explanation: Athetoid cerebral palsy shows slow, involuntary, uncontrolled movements.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A patient status post CVA rocks back and forth in a supine position with legs flexed and arms clasped around his knees. Expected therapeutic outcomes include all of the following except:

options.A: Decreased extensor spasticity in the lower extremities
options.B: Inhibition of flexor spasticity in the upper extremities
options.D: Facilitation of extensor tone in the trunk

questions.explanation: Rocking with knees clasped does not facilitate trunk extensor tone; it inhibits spasticity and promotes protraction.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A development examination is completed on an eight month old infant. Findings from the examination include: the patient brings hands to mouth, requires assistance for ring sitting, presents with slight head lag, and does not reach across midline for objects. This child appears: Exercise Therapy 19
questions.explanation: At eight months an infant should sit unsupported and have no head lag, so the findings indicate delay.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: Facilitation of muscle tone is performed through all of the following except:
questions.explanation: Maintained pressure is an inhibitory technique; approximation, vibration and quick icing facilitate.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A therapist completes an initial examination on a patient diagnosed with complete C7 tetrapegia. The patient problem list includes the following: inability to complete an independent bed to wheelchair transfer, decreased passive lower extremity range of motion tissue breakdown over the ischial tuberosities, and decreased upper extremity strength. Which of the following treatment activities should be given the highest priority?

options.B: Transfer training using a sliding board

questions.explanation: Pressure relief is the priority when tissue breakdown is present over the ischial tuberosities.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A therapist completes a developmental assessment on a five-month-old infant. If the therapist elects to examine the infant's palmar grasp reflex, which of the following stimuli is the most appropriate?

options.A: Contact to the ball of the foot in upright standing
options.B: Maintained pressure to the palm of the hand
options.C: Noxious stimulus to the palm of the hand
options.D: Sudden change in the position of the hand

questions.explanation: The palmar grasp reflex is elicited by maintained pressure to the palm.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A therapist examines a patient status post-traumatic brain injury. Then examining neurologic tone the most appropriate method is:

options.A: Active range of motion of the involved extremities
options.B: Passive range of motion of the involved extremities
options.C: Passive range of motion of the involved and uninvolved extremities
options.D: Resisted motion of the involved extremities

questions.explanation: Tone should be compared between the involved and uninvolved sides.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A therapist completes a developmental assessment on a three month old child. Which reflex is simulated by the head suddenly dropping into extension?
questions.explanation: Sudden head drop into extension elicits the Moro reflex.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: When treating a patient with hemiplegia in tall kneeling, which treatment technique would be the least effective?

options.A: Proprioceptive neuromuscular facilitation "chopping" in D1, D2
options.B: Reaching across midline with the unaffected arm
options.C: Reaching across midline with the hands in prayer position
options.D: Straight plane motion with the unaffected arm

questions.explanation: Straight-plane movements of the unaffected arm do little to challenge trunk rotation or weight shift.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A physical therapist a one month old infant. During the treatment session the therapist strokes the cheek of the infant causing the infant to turn its mouth towards the stimulus. This action best defines the __________ reflex?
questions.explanation: Stroking the cheek causing head turning toward the stimulus is the rooting reflex.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: The treatment plan for a patient with hemiplegia includes reinforcing normal movement through key points of control and avoiding all reflex movement patterns and associated reactions. This approach most closely resembles: Exercise Therapy 21
questions.explanation: Reinforcing normal movement through key points of control is the Bobath concept.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A physical therapist examines a patient with multiple sclerosis. The therapist documents that the patient presents with dysdiadochokinesia. Which objective finding is most representative of dysdiadochokinesia?

options.A: Inability to perform rapid alternating movements
options.B: Inability to discriminate selected tactile input
options.D: Presence of involuntary, rhythmic, and oscillatory movements at rest

questions.explanation: Dysdiadochokinesia is inability to perform rapid alternating movements.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)
questions.sourceChapter: Cited reference: Physical Rehabilitation/O'Sullivan/4th Ed./ Pg. 740

questions.question: Which of the following developmental milestones is usually not observed when examining a four month old infant?

options.C: Transfers blocks from one hand to the other
options.D: Holds head erect when held in a sitting position

questions.explanation: Transferring objects hand to hand appears at about six months, not four.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: The intermittent use of tone reducing lower extremity bivalve casting for children with cerebral palsy hypothesizes that casting may:

options.B: Cause flexion of the toes which inhibits the plantar grasp response
options.C: Facilitate trunk stability by reducing contractures of the foot
options.D: Inhibit the use of extensor thrust by preventing plantar flexion

questions.explanation: Bivalve casting inhibits extensor thrust by preventing plantar flexion.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A therapist treats a patient status post CVA. Which action would be most likely to facilitate elbow extension in a patient with hemiplegia?

options.A: Turn the head o the affected side
options.B: Turn the head to the unaffected side

questions.explanation: Turning the head toward the affected side uses the asymmetrical tonic neck reflex to facilitate extension.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A patient with hemiplegia lying in supine demonstrates a synergistic pattern of movement when attempting to move his affected leg. The patient's hip is abducted and externally related knee flexed, ankle plantar flexed and inverted, toes plantar flexed and classified as:

options.C: A combination of flexion and extension on a pattern with

questions.explanation: The pattern combines flexion at the hip and knee with abduction and external rotation; it is a mixed synergy pattern.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A 35-year-old patient, six months status post CVA and right hemiparesis, attends physical therapy on an outpatient basis. As the patient lies supine on the mat, the therapist applies resistance to right elbow flexion. The therapist notes mass flexion of the right lower extremity as the resistance applied. The therapist should document this as:
questions.explanation: Mass flexion of the leg during resisted elbow flexion is homolateral synkinesis.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A child with athetoid cerebral palsy is referred to physical therapy. Which of the following characteristics 22 would a physical therapist typically identify when examining the child?

options.A: Continuous low tone and intermittent tonic spasms
options.B: Small range movements with full control within the range
options.C: Disorganized movement with fluctuating muscle tone
options.D: Little to no influence from tonic neck reflexes

questions.explanation: Athetoid cerebral palsy shows disorganised movement with fluctuating tone.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A patient begins to demonstrate signs and symptoms of a seizure including uncontrollable muscular movements, convulsions, and confused behavior. Appropriate intervention would include:

options.A: Attempt to check airway breathing and circulation
options.B: Place a soft object between the patient's teeth
options.D: Protect the victim from injury, but do not restrain

questions.explanation: During a seizure the patient is protected from injury but not restrained.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A physical therapist conducts an initial examination on a patient diagnosed with Parkinson's disease. Which of the following clinical findings would you expect the therapist to identify?
questions.explanation: Cogwheel rigidity is characteristic of Parkinson's disease.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A 63-year-old female status post stroke is screened for admission into a rehabilitation hospital. A part of the screen the therapist utilizes a standardized instrument to document the extent of the patient's impairments and disabilities. Which of the following standardized instruments would be most beneficial to provide an assessment of motor function?
questions.explanation: The Fugl-Meyer Assessment documents motor impairment after stroke.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A physical therapist reviews an initial examination of a patient diagnosed with an upper motor neuron disease. The examination documents the existence of a positive Babinski reflex. A positive Babinski reflex is characterized by:
questions.explanation: A positive Babinski is extension of the great toe.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A physical therapist examines a patient with lower extremity hypertonicity. All of the following could be used by the therapist to temporarily reduce tone except:
questions.explanation: Approximation facilitates tone; rocking, cold and sustained stretch reduce it.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A physical therapist positions a patient with hemiplegia in a plantigrade position to promote weight bearing through the affected upper extremity. The most appropriate hand position on the plinth is:

options.A: Total palmar contact with the fingers fully extended
options.B: Total plamar contact with fingers flexed
options.C: Weight bearing on a closed fist
options.D: Palmar contact with support of the palmar arches and weight through the heel of the hand

questions.explanation: Weight bearing through the heel of the hand with the palmar arches supported is the correct hand position.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A patient demonstrates unilateral neglect to the left. The physical therapist's short term goals for the patient include reducing the patient's neglect. Which treatment technique would not be effective in improving the patient's condition?

options.A: Have the patient participate in bilateral tasks to increase total body awareness
options.B: Place the patient's food on the right side of the tray so the patient can eat by himself
options.C: Have the patient observe himself massaging his left upper extremity
options.D: Have the patient use a mirror while dressing

questions.explanation: Placing food on the right side encourages the patient to ignore the neglected left side.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A physical therapist attempts to have a patient status post CVA reach for a cone by moving her trunk away from midline. The most appropriate type of manual contact to assist the patient with the movement is:
questions.explanation: Light intermittent touch is used to guide movement away from midline without creating dependence.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A physical therapist would not expect a seven month old infant to have completed which of the following developmental milestones?
questions.explanation: Forward crawling is not expected by seven months.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: During an examination of a patient with a traumatic brain injury a therapist notes the patient mumbling phrases which are nonpurposeful in nature. As the physical therapist initiates passive range of motion to the patient's lower extremities, the patient attempts to strike the therapist in the head. According to the Ranchos los Amigos levels of cognitive functioning, the patient would be best described at level:
questions.explanation: Non-purposeful mumbling with striking out is Rancho level IV (confused-agitated).
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A patient with right hemiplegia is observed during gait training. The patient performs side stepping towards the hemiplegic side. The physical therapist may expect the patient to compensate for weakened abductors by:

options.A: Hip hiking of the unaffected side
options.B: Lateral trunk flexion towards the hemiplegic side
options.C: Lateral trunk flexion towards the unaffected side
options.D: Hip extension of the hemiplegic side 24

questions.explanation: Weak abductors are compensated by lateral trunk flexion toward the unaffected side.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: The rate of pin rolling tremors in Parkinson's disease is:
questions.explanation: Pill-rolling tremor occurs at about 4 to 8 cycles per second.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A therapist identifies that a child is unable to roll from prone to supine. Which reflex could most interfere with the child's ability to roll?
questions.explanation: The asymmetrical tonic neck reflex can interfere with rolling.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A therapist develops a plan of care for a patient with hemiplegia. What is the primary purpose of using a sling in the management of a subluxed shoulder?

options.A: Correct the cause of the subluxation
options.D: To hold the upper extremity in proper alignment

questions.explanation: A sling holds the arm in alignment but does not correct the subluxation.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A physical therapist reviews the initial examination of a patient diagnosed with a cerebellar CVA. The therapist might expect the patient's primary impairment to be:
questions.explanation: Gait and balance disturbance is the main impairment of a cerebellar stroke.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A therapist completes an examination on a young girl with spastic cerebral palsy. The therapist determines that the girl has involvement in all four extremities as well as the head, neck, and trunk. What type of cerebral palsy classification best describes the girl's condition?
questions.explanation: Involvement of all four limbs, head, neck and trunk is spastic tetraplegia (quadriplegia).
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A patient diagnosed with Parkinson's disease has difficulty initiating movement. What proprioceptive neuromuscular facilitation technique would be most appropriate to treat this problem?
questions.explanation: Rhythmic initiation helps patients with Parkinson's disease start movement.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A physical therapist instructs a patient to move from sit- ting through quadruped to tall kneeling. By moving through the developmental sequence a patient gains ____ control dur- ing movement and ___ during static positioning?
questions.explanation: Moving through developmental postures trains isotonic control during movement and isometric control in static positions.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: The long-term goal of a patients status post CVA is to walk to work. Which of the following conditions would serve as the largest obstacle to the patient achieving the goal?
questions.explanation: Homonymous hemianopia is the greatest obstacle to safe community walking.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A physical therapist examines a patient with right hemiplegia four days status post CVA. All of the following would be appropriate short term goals excepts:

options.B: Initiate activities of daily living with assistance
options.C: Demonstrate awareness of the hemiplegic side through positioning
options.D: Perform lower extremity exercises without assistance

questions.explanation: Performing exercises without assistance is not a realistic goal four days after stroke.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)
questions.sourceChapter: Cited reference: Physical Rehabilitation/O'Sullivan/4th Ed./ Pg. 544-545

questions.question: A patient status post CVA with abnormal tone on the right side lies supine in bed. The patient's physical therapist iscourage her from lying supine for long periods of time because:

options.A: The position can cause shoulder-hand syndrome
options.B: The position increases an inferior subluxation
options.C: The position encourages tonic neck and labyrinthine reflexes
options.D: The position increase stone in the pectoralis 26

questions.explanation: Prolonged supine lying encourages tonic neck and labyrinthine reflex activity.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: Gower's sign is seen in:
questions.explanation: Gowers' sign is seen in Duchenne muscular dystrophy.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: Berg balance test for balance assessment is most suitable in which age group patients?
questions.explanation: The Berg Balance Scale is designed mainly for older adults.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: Gower's sign is apparent during which of following position?
questions.explanation: Gowers' sign is seen when rising from sitting or lying to standing.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A physical therapy record indicates a patient exhibits dysdiadochokinesia. Based on the patient's documented deficit, which test would you expect to be the most difficult for the patient?
questions.explanation: Dysdiadochokinesia makes alternating pronation and supination most difficult.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A treatment program is designed to include late morning sessions involving aggressive stretching moderate exercise, energy conservation, and stress management techniques. This program would be most appropriate for which diagnosis?
questions.explanation: Late-morning treatment with energy conservation fits myasthenia gravis, when medication effect is at its best.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A physical therapist examines a patient with shoulder subluxation secondary to a flaccid upper extremity. The therapist's short term goal is to prevent further subluxation. The following techniques would be beneficial in treating the flaccid upper extremity except:

options.D: Arm support when sitting and standing

questions.explanation: Distraction and stretching worsen subluxation in a flaccid shoulder.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A physical therapist uses rhythmic initiation to assist a patient in learning to roll from supine to prone. The physical therapist's initial command should be:

options.C: Stop me from rolling you over
options.D: Relax and let me move you

questions.explanation: Rhythmic initiation begins with relaxed passive movement ("relax and let me move you").
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: Most useful modality for rehabilitation in cervical spine injury with quadriplegia is:
questions.explanation: A tilt table helps adapt to the upright posture after cervical cord injury.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A patient with a T6 spinal cord injury prepares for discharge from a rehabilitation center following 15 weeks of intensive therapy. Which of the following does not accurately describe the patient's expected functional ability at the conclusion of rehabilitation?

options.A: Independent in light housekeeping and meal preparation
options.B: Independent bowel and bladder care with appropriate equipment
options.D: Independent ambulation with forearm crutches and bilateral knee-ankle-food orthoses 54

questions.explanation: Independent ambulation with KAFOs and crutches is not a functional expectation after T6 injury.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A therapist orders a wheelchair for a patient with T8-T9 paraplegia. Which wheelchair option is not usually necessary for a patient with paraplegia?
questions.explanation: Handrim projections are not usually needed in paraplegia.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A therapist works on range of motion of the lower extremities with a patient rehabilitating from spinal cord injury. Independent range of motion of the lower extremities is a realistic goal for which spinal cord level?
questions.explanation: Independent lower-limb range of motion is realistic at C7 and below.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A therapist examines a patient with a C5 spinal cord injury. A realistic goal for the patient is:

options.B: Forward raise in wheelchair using loops for pressure relief
options.C: Independent rolling from prone to supine and supine to prone

questions.explanation: A realistic goal at C5 is forward raise using loops for pressure relief.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: The following description best describes a patient with a spinal cord injury at the ____ level? Biceps, deltoids, and rotator cuff musculature are intact. Independent transfers with a sliding board may be possible.
questions.explanation: Intact biceps, deltoids and rotator cuff with possible sliding-board transfers describes C6.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A realistic long term goal for a patient with T10 paraplegia is:

options.A: The patient is able to ambulate with bilateral knee-anklefoot orthoses using forearm crutches and a four-point gait pattern
options.B: The patient is able to ambulate with bilateral ankle-foot orthoses using forearm crutches and a three-point gait pattern
options.C: The patient is able to ambulate with bilateral knee-ankle-foot orthoses using forearm crutches and a swing-to gait pattern
options.D: The patient is able to ambulate independently in the parallel bars with bilateral ankle-foot orthoses and a swing-to gait pattern

questions.explanation: T10 paraplegia can ambulate with bilateral KAFOs and forearm crutches.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A therapist orders a wheelchair for a patient with C4 tetraplegia. Which power wheelchair option would be inappropriate for the patient?
questions.explanation: Hand controls are inappropriate for C4 tetraplegia; sip-and-puff or chin controls are used.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A respiratory examination is performed on a patient with tetraplegia with the following results: the patient attains seventy percent of standard vital capacity, he is able to verbalize eight syllables per breath, and is able to mobilize and clear secretions from his longs. Which level of injury does this best describe?
questions.explanation: Seventy percent vital capacity and effective secretion clearance fits C7-C8.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A therapist develops a chart detailing expected functional outcomes for a variety of spinal cord injuries. Which is the highest spinal level at which independent transfers with sliding board would be feasible?
questions.explanation: C6 is the highest level for independent sliding-board transfers.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A patient with complete C5 tetraplegia works on a forward raise for pressure relief with his therapist. The patient utilizes loops that are attached to the back of the wheelchair to assist with successful with the forward raise:
questions.explanation: Biceps and deltoids pull the body forward in the C5 forward raise using loops.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A therapist treats a patient with complete C6 tetraplegia. Which of the following would not be an expected functional outcome for the patient?

options.A: Independent transfers with a sliding board
options.B: Independent bowel and balder care Biomechanics 55

questions.explanation: Independent bowel and bladder care is not expected at C6.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: Which statement best describes the realistic functional status of a patient with C4 tetraplegia after completing rehabilitation?

options.B: Independent in all activities of daily living
options.C: Able to propel a manual wheelchair independently
options.D: Able to operate a power wheelchair

questions.explanation: C4 tetraplegia can operate a power wheelchair.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A therapist orders a wheelchair for a patient in a rehabilitation hospital. Which of the following patients would be most in need of a wheelchair with handrim projections?

options.A: A patient with a C3 spinal cord injury
options.B: A patient with a C5 spinal cord injury
options.D: A patient with a cauda equina lesion

questions.explanation: Handrim projections help patients with C5 injury propel a wheelchair.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A therapist examines a patient with a C6 spinal cord injury. Which muscle would not be innervated based on the patient's level of injury?
questions.explanation: Triceps (C7) is not innervated in a C6 injury.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: At what level is it realistic for a patient with a spinal cord injury to functionally ambulate?
questions.explanation: Functional ambulation is realistic from about L1 downward.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A therapist measures a patient for a wheelchair. Which measurement is used to determine armrest height in a wheelchair?

options.A: Seat to anterior superior iliac spine

questions.explanation: Armrest height is set from seat to olecranon.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A patient status post stroke presents with a hypotonic left upper extremity. While performing sitting activities the position of choice for the left upper extremity is:

options.C: Weight bearing through the upper extremity with the elbow extended
options.D: Weight bearing through the upper extremity with the elbow and wrist flexed

questions.explanation: Weight bearing with the elbow extended supports a hypotonic arm.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)
